look_here_first: Start with the fruit: black walnut has by far the largest fruit in this trio, usually about 3.5–8 cm, and the nut surface between the deep grooves is coarsely warty. Mature trees can also become dramatically taller and heavier-trunked.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: nut about 3–4 cm, deeply grooved with coarsely warty surface between grooves

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: dark deeply ridged bark on mature trees

lookalikes.differences: J. major has smaller 2–3.5 cm fruit with smoother nut surfaces between grooves; J. microcarpa has tiny fruit and many very narrow leaflets.
